summary: Split the PRD into three markdown sections: problem/goal & users, functional requirements & input data, non‑functional requirements & milestones

shared.style_guide: Use plain short sentences. No marketing words or emojis. Active voice, sentence case, single space after periods. Paragraphs separated by a blank line. Bulleted lists use hyphens. Numbered lists use digits followed by a period. All headings start with ## for sections and ### for subsections. No HTML tags, images, or external links.
shared.heading_levels: Each component starts with a level‑2 heading (##). Any deeper heading is level‑3 (###).

components.purpose: Provide the problem statement, goal, and user use cases
components.spec: Start with a level‑2 heading "## Problem and Goal {.fa-section}". Include a paragraph that reads exactly "The trace screen currently draws agents as a flat graph. When a swarm of 3 to 24 agents is shown the graph becomes unreadable." Follow with a line "Goal: add a swarm view with one lane per worker agent, showing the agent's task, progress and result." Add a level‑3 heading "### Users and Use Cases {.fa-section}". Under it place a bulleted list with three items: "- Live demo to a visitor", "- Replay of a saved run", "- Debugging a failed worker". No other content.

components.purpose: List functional requirements and describe the required input data
components.spec:
Begin with a level‑2 heading "## Functional Requirements {.fa-section}". Follow with a numbered list prefixed with FR‑ and a period. Include exactly six items: 
1. FR-1. Display a separate lane for each worker agent.
2. FR-2. Show the agent's task text in the lane.
3. FR-3. Show progress state as a percentage.
4. FR-4. Show token counter and millisecond counter.
5. FR-5. Allow clicking a lane to open a fragment of the trace.
6. FR-6. Number each requirement with the FR- prefix.
Add a level‑3 heading "### Input Data {.fa-section}". Include a single paragraph that reads exactly "The view consumes trace format v2 events only: run_start, agent_spawn, llm_start, llm_end, tool_start, tool_end, run_end." No other text.

components.purpose: Define non‑functional requirements, out‑of‑scope items, and milestones with acceptance criteria
components.spec:
Start with a level‑2 heading "## Non-functional Requirements {.fa-section}". Follow with a numbered list prefixed with NFR‑ and a period containing three items: 
1. NFR-1. Render at 60 fps with up to 24 agents.
2. NFR-2. Work offline on replay.
3. NFR-3. Use plain black text on white background.
Add a level‑3 heading "### Out of Scope and Open Questions {.fa-section}". Include a bulleted list with exactly two items: "- No support for more than 24 agents.", "- How to handle dynamic agent addition after start.".
Add a level‑3 heading "### Milestones and Acceptance {.fa-section}". Provide three milestone entries, each on its own line:
- M1: Basic lane rendering. Acceptance: "M1 demo shows 3 lanes with static task text."
- M2: Progress counters. Acceptance: "M2 demo shows token and ms counters updating in real time."
- M3: Full interaction. Acceptance: "M3 demo shows clicking a lane opens the corresponding trace fragment."
